full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque, J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why granting of full relief by respondent No. 5 by allowing time barred Appeal Case No. 125119 of 2009 (Annexure-D) on merit filed under Rule 31 of East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 against the order of dismissal for default passed in Objection Case No. 978 of 2005 under Rule 30 of East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 (Annexure-C) by the respondent No. 3 for revising the record of right in the name of mother of the petitioners should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Shorn of unnecessary details, fact of the case lies in a very narrow compas. Respondent Nos. 6-8 filed Objection Case No. 978 of 2005 under Rule 30 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 ("Rules") before the settlement officer against the record of right stands in the name of the petitioners' mother. The case was dismissed for default on 13-12-2006. Thereafter, petitioner of objection case did not take any step either by way of restoration of the objection case or any other steps for long time rather the petitioner preferred appeal under Rules 31of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules at the end of the year 2009 without application for condonation of delay. After filing of the appeal the appellate officer vide its order No. 4 dated 13-12-2003 observed that the appeal has not been filed within time, as such, it requires condonation of delay and sent the record to Officer-in-Charge, Keshobpur, Jessore for hearing and disposal. After receiving record, the Officer-in-Charge issued notice to the parties fixing on 23-12-2015 for hearing. On the date fixed the appellate officer did not dispose of the matter condonation of delay, but observed that the delay was condoned on earlier date and he took up the matter for hearing and upon hearing by the order dated 23-11-2015 allowed the appeal and set-aside the order of the settlement officer.
